items.title: Tracking water use on construction sites
items.description: Water meters were read by hand. With LoRaWAN, GPS, and a dashboard, project managers now see usage live, without walking the site.

treepin.context: Greenlightbeheer is a specialized tree care service that inspects thousands of trees for municipalities, private landowners, and companies. Inspectors work in the field; managers plan follow-up actions; clients (municipalities) want visibility into their tree inventory.
treepin.problem: Inspectors worked with paper, camera, and GPS notes. No central overview, no per-tree history, no risk prioritization. Data had to be hand-entered, causing errors. Clients couldn't see what was happening. Each inspection cost €50–150 due to inefficiency.
treepin.approach: We examined how fieldwork actually operates: inspectors must work offline, data syncs when they return, maps help with route planning, managers need real-time status. Choice: Next.js webapp (desktop/tablet), Capacitor for offline tablet mode, Supabase for auth + real-time sync, Mapbox for geo-visualization.
treepin.solution: Next.js 16 webapp with React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS. Capacitor 8 for Android tablet app (offline-capable, keep-awake). Supabase backend (PostgreSQL, Auth, RLS, Realtime). Mapbox GL + Leaflet for map visualization. Photo upload via Resend; optional Google Cloud Vision for analysis. Role management (technician/manager/client read-only), audit logs. Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + Capacitor 8 + Supabase + Mapbox GL.
treepin.outcome: Greenlightbeheer fully digitizes tree inspections. Inspectors enter data on-site; data syncs in real-time. Cost per inspection dropped from €50–150 to €10–30. Managers see live status and can optimize route planning. Clients (including city of Maldegem) now have an up-to-date, searchable inventory with risk prioritization and automatic follow-up scheduling. Complete audit trail for compliance.

studio-huis.context: Studio Huis guides homeowners in Flanders through smarter renovations: renovation advice, energy & EPC, interior and lighting advice, and digital home dossiers. The practice needed a website that turns expertise into a clear, approachable journey.
studio-huis.problem: Without a sharp digital presence, the offer lived mostly in conversations and ad-hoc explanations. Visitors couldn’t quickly see how the approach works, which services exist, or how to take a first step — so leads and trust were left on the table.
studio-huis.approach: We started from one clear promise — smart renovating starts here — and built a brand-first landing: hero, step-by-step approach, services with concrete deliverables, and a contact form with privacy consent. Focus First kept scope tight: persuade and convert, no unnecessary modules.
studio-huis.solution: A marketing site on a modern Next.js stack with responsive layout, clear CTAs, service structure (renovation, energy/EPC, interior & light, digital home dossier), and an intake form. Content and UX tuned for homeowners who don’t know where to start.
studio-huis.outcome: studiohuis.be is live as both a recognizable digital calling card and a lead channel. Visitors see in one viewport who Studio Huis is, how the journey works, and can share their situation immediately.

greenlight-beheer.context: Greenlight BV is a certified study & consultancy practice in Meise for forest, park, nature, and tree management (including European Tree Technician & VETcert), with a 25-year path from tree care to broader green advice — including Treepin as a digital product.
greenlight-beheer.problem: Expertise and services (management advice, tree expertise, Natura 2000, timber sales, poplar cultivation, execution) were strong in the field, but not clearly bundled online. Public and private clients needed a professional, trust-building starting point.
greenlight-beheer.approach: We positioned Greenlight as a study & consultancy with natural imagery, certification badges, and a clear services grid. Treepin and partners got a place in navigation without crowding out the core — advice and guidance.
greenlight-beheer.solution: A corporate website with full-bleed hero, service cards, about section, client segments, and contact CTA. Responsive, SEO-friendly basics (title/description), and links into the wider ecosystem (including Treepin).
greenlight-beheer.outcome: greenlightbeheer.be makes 25 years of experience and the service portfolio visible to governments, forest groups, and private owners — with a professional first impression that matches the fieldwork and digital tools.

multiplugin.context: Furniture makers work in SketchUp from mass box (client proposal) to technical build-out. The core question: how do you reduce repeatable cabinet steps to a single click — without losing grip on materials and cost?
multiplugin.problem: Going from box to corpus or from a flat face to a door meant hours of manual copying, measuring, and tagging. Material lists lived outside the model — error-prone for production and cost calculation.
multiplugin.approach: Key idea: one-click actions. We built Multiplugin platform around actions that deliver in a single click — box → full corpus, flat face → finished door — tied to a tag system and an external platform for materials and cost.
multiplugin.solution: SketchUp Ruby plugin with wizards like ‘Box to corpus’ (dimensions, materials, division, fronts) and Multitag filter (parts, quantities, m², lm). External web platform (Next.js + Supabase) for material management and cost calculation; API sync so the material list from the model matches the catalog.
multiplugin.outcome: Makers turn a mass box into a full corpus — or a flat face into a finished door — in one click. Tags and quantities feed the material list on the external platform immediately — for management and costing, without double entry.

iot-water-meters.context: Construction sites install temporary water meters for billing and usage tracking. Projects run for months, and water consumption fluctuates by phase — so accurate readings are essential for correct billing and budget control.
iot-water-meters.problem: Meter readings were taken by hand — error-prone, time-consuming, and a common source of billing disputes. Project managers only saw daily figures, not real-time usage or anomalies.
iot-water-meters.approach: We explored what sensor data was already available per meter, how it could be collected automatically with minimal hardware, and how live insight was possible without on-site visits. We chose low-power sensors and cloud storage.
iot-water-meters.solution: LoRaWAN sensors (each with built-in GPS) on every meter, connected via existing LoRa gateways, parsed to AWS IoT Core and visualized in a custom React dashboard. Anomaly detection with threshold alerts. Backend: Node.js, PostgreSQL, MapBox for GPS visualization.
iot-water-meters.outcome: Beta tested on 3 construction sites over 8 weeks. Within the first month: fewer billing disputes (data is now factual and timestamped), faster invoice processing, and project managers see real-time consumption patterns so they can intervene when something's off.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.content: Focus First respects your privacy. This privacy policy describes how we collect, use, and protect personal data under the GDPR.

sections.heading: 2. Data Controller
sections.content: The data controller is Jonathan Barbé, trading as Focus First Digital Lab. Address: J.Hammeneckerstraat 40, 1880 Kapelle-op-den-Bos, Belgium. VAT: BE 0881.296.468. Contact: info@focusfirst.be. Website: www.focusfirst.be.

sections.heading: 3. Data We Collect
sections.content: We collect data you voluntarily provide through contact forms: name, email address, organization type, project description. With consent, we also collect aggregated usage statistics via Google Analytics.

sections.heading: 4. How We Use Your Data
sections.content: Your data is used to contact you about your project, send quotes, and deliver projects. Legal bases: consent (form) and/or legitimate interest for responding to your inquiry.

sections.heading: 5. Processors and transfers
sections.content: We use Resend for email delivery and, only with your consent, Google Analytics (Google Ireland / Google LLC). Analytics may process data outside the EU under appropriate safeguards (including Standard Contractual Clauses). We do not share contact data for marketing.

sections.heading: 6. Cookies and Tracking
sections.content: Non-essential analytics cookies are only set after consent via the cookie banner. Details are in the cookie policy. You can change your choice later via Cookie settings in the footer.

sections.heading: 7. Your Rights (GDPR)
sections.content: You have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict, object, and data portability. Contact info@focusfirst.be. You may also lodge a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (GBA).

sections.heading: 8. Retention Period
sections.content: We retain contact information as long as needed for the project and up to 1 year afterward, unless you request deletion. Analytics data follows Google Analytics retention (default up to 14 months).

sections.heading: 1. Applicability
sections.content: These terms apply to all services of Jonathan Barbé, trading as Focus First Digital Lab (VAT BE 0881.296.468), J.Hammeneckerstraat 40, 1880 Kapelle-op-den-Bos, Belgium.

sections.heading: 2. Quotes and Contracts
sections.content: Quotes are non-binding. A project begins after written confirmation and contract signature.

sections.heading: 3. Payment
sections.content: Payments follow the terms stated in the project contract. Focus First reserves the right to stop work if payment is not made.

sections.heading: 4. Intellectual Property Rights
sections.content: Delivered code and designs are owned by the client after full payment.

sections.heading: 5. Support and Warranty
sections.content: 30 days of post-launch support is included in Digital+ and Smart+ packages. Afterward, support is available on a project basis.

sections.heading: 6. Liability
sections.content: Focus First is not liable for indirect damages. Direct liability is limited to the project fee.

sections.heading: 7. Changes
sections.content: Scope or timeline changes are possible and will be billed separately.

sections.heading: 1. What Are Cookies?
sections.content: Cookies are small text files stored on your device. We also use similar technologies such as localStorage for your cookie preference.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Cookies We Use
sections.content: Essential: cookie consent storage (localStorage key cookie-consent, until cleared). Analytics (consent only): Google Analytics (_ga, _ga_*, typically up to 2 years, provider: Google). Marketing: none.

sections.heading: 3. Google Analytics
sections.content: With consent we use GA4 for aggregated statistics (page views, traffic). Consent Mode defaults to denied; analytics cookies activate only after you accept. We do not set advertising/remarketing cookies.

sections.heading: 4. Your Choice
sections.content: On first visit you choose via the banner. Rejecting is as easy as accepting. You can change your choice later via Cookie settings in the footer.

sections.heading: 5. Recommendation
sections.content: Analytics helps us improve the site, but is always optional. Essential functionality works without analytics cookies.
